• **GST 2.0 introduces a streamlined tax structure with two main slabs of 5% and 18%, along with a 40% demerit rate for sin and luxury goods**. The reforms emphasize tax reductions on essential items, healthcare, and automobiles. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

• **New Structure**: **Two-slab GST** system of **5%** and** 18%**, with a **special 40% demerit rate for super-luxury and sin goods.**
 
• **Implementation Date**: All rate changes (except tobacco) effective from September 22, 2025 (Navratri’s first day).
 
• **GST-Free Items:** UHT milk, paneer, pizza bread, chapati, khakra, parathas, erasers.
 
• **Food & Daily Use Items:** Packaged food (juices, butter, cheese, pasta, nuts, sauces, chocolates, instant noodles, namkeens, coffee) now at 5%.

• **Healthcare Support**: Vision correction spectacles cut to 5% (from 28%).
 
• **Insurance**: Life and health insurance policies made GST-exempt.
 
• **Services**: Gyms, salons, barbers, yoga services reduced from 18% to 5%.
 
• **White Goods & Autos:**
 
 
• **ACs, TVs, dishwashers** → 18% (from 28%).
 
• **Small cars** (petrol ≤1200cc, diesel ≤1500cc), motorcycles ≤350cc, auto parts → 18%.

• **EVs **remain at 5%.
 
• **Infrastructure**: Cement cut from 28% → 18%.
 
 
 
• **Sectoral Reforms:**
 
 
• **Textiles**: Manmade fibre (18% → 5%), yarn (12% → 5%).
 
• **Fertilisers**: Ammonia, sulphuric acid, nitric acid (18% → 5%).
 
 
 
• **Luxury/Sin Goods**: 40% GST slab includes pan masala, gutka, zarda, tobacco products, caffeinated beverages, yachts, helicopters, private-use airplanes, large motorcycles (>350cc).
 
• **Revenue Concerns:** States raised ₹80,000–1.5 lakh crore loss fears; Centre estimated net fiscal impact of ₹48,000 crore.
 
• **Industry Reaction:** CII and industry groups welcomed reforms; expected to ease compliance, reduce litigation, boost demand, and create jobs.

questions.question: In India, palm, coconut, keora, agar are the common trees of which of the following forests?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Mangrove Forests**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Mangrove Forests

__
 
• Found in the areas of coasts influenced by tides. Mud and silt get accumulated on such coasts.
 
• Dense mangroves are the common varieties with roots of the plants submerged underwater.
 
• The deltas of the Ganga, the Mahanadi, the Krishana, the Godavari, and the Kaveri are covered by such vegetation.
 
• In the Ganga Brahmaputra delta, Sundari trees are found, which provide durable hard timber.
 
• Palm, coconut, keora, agar, also grow in some parts of the delta.
 
• Royal Bengal Tiger is the famous animal in these forests. Turtles, crocodiles, gharials, and snakes are also found in these forests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__Tropical Evergreen Forests:__

 
• These forests are restricted to heavy rainfall areas of the *Western Ghats and the island groups of Lakshadweep, Andaman, and Nicobar, upper parts of Assam, and Tamil Nadu coast.*
 
• They are at their best in areas having more than 200 cm of rainfall with a short dry season.
 
• The trees reach great heights up to 60 meters or even above.
 
• Since the region is warm and wet throughout the year, it has luxuriant vegetation of all kinds.
 
• The trees, shrubs, and creepers give it a multilayered structure.
 
• There is no definite time for trees to shed their leaves.
 
• As such, these forests appear green all the year-round

Tropical Deciduous Forests

 
• ​These are the most widespread forests of India.
 
• They are also called the monsoon forests and spread over the region receiving rainfall between 200 cm and 70 cm.
 
• Trees of this forest type shed their leaves for about six to eight weeks in dry summer.
 
• On the basis of the availability of water, these forests are further divided into moist and dry deciduous.

Natural vegetation refers to a plant community, which has grown naturally without human aid and has been left undisturbed by humans for a long time. The following major types of vegetation may be identified in our country

 
• Tropical Evergreen Forests
 
• Tropical Deciduous Forests
 
• Tropical Thorn Forests and Scrubs
 
• Montane Forests
 
• Mangrove Forests

questions.question: Which latitude line passes through the middle of India influencing the climate of the country?

__
 
• The Tropic of Cancer passes through eight states in India: Gujarat (Jasdan), Rajasthan (Kalinjarh), Madhya Pradesh (Shajapur), Chhattisgarh (Sonhat), Jharkhand (Lohardaga), West Bengal (Krishnanagar), Tripura (Udaipur), and Mizoram (Champhai).
 
• The Tropic of Cancer is a parallel of latitude on the Earth, 23.5 degrees north of the equator.
 
• Mahi River is the only river in India that cuts the Tropic of Cancer twice, first in Madhya Pradesh from where it flows towards Rajasthan and enters Gujarat where it cuts for the second time.

• It is halfway between the North Pole and the South Pole, at 0 degrees latitude.
 
• An equator divides the planet into a Northern Hemisphere and a Southern Hemisphere.

**Tropic of Capricorn**

 
• This latitude corresponds to the southernmost declination of the Sun's ecliptic to the celestial equator.
 
• Latitude approximately 23°27′ S of the terrestrial Equator.

• **The Krishna River** is one of the major rivers in **India, flowing through the states of Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• It does flow through t**he Deccan Plateau,** but it's not the river that traditionally marks the northern boundary of the plateau.
 
 
 
• **Tapi:**

questions.question: Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment under a peepal tree at _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bodh Gaya. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gautama Buddha **attained** enlightenment **under a **peepal tree at Bodh Gaya, **which is located in the Indian state of** Bihar.**
 
• The peepal tree under which Buddha attained enlightenment is also known as the **Bodhi Tree, **which is considered **sacred by Buddhists.**
 
• **Bodh Gaya is home to the Mahabodhi Temple, **which was built by** Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE** to commemorate Buddha's enlightenment
 
• **The Mahabodhi Temple complex **also** includes the Vajrasana,** which is believed to be the spot where Buddha meditated and attained enlightenment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Important events in the life of Gautama Buddha:**

 
• The Buddha, initially known as **Siddhartha Gautama,** was born into a royal family in **Lumbini,** currently located in **Nepal, in the 6th to 4th century BCE.**
 
• At the age of 29, after witnessing the sufferings of life (old age, sickness, death), Gautama renounced his royal life in **search of the path to end human suffering.**
 
• For several years, he embraced the life of an ascetic, practicing extreme austerity. However, he found this didn't lead to enlightenment and instead advocated for what he called** "the Middle Way"**—a life of moderation away from extreme asceticism and hedonism.
 
• After attaining enlightenment, the Buddha delivered his **first sermon in Sarnath**, near **Varanasi in India**, often referred to as **"Setting the Wheel of Dhamma in Motion**". It marked the beginning of his teaching or the dissemination of his understanding of the "truth" about life and existence.
 
• Buddha initiated a community of followers, both **monks (Bhikkus) and nuns (Bhikkunis).** This Buddhist monastic community, known as Sangha, spread the teachings of Buddha after his death.
 
• The Buddha died at the **age of 80, in Kushinagar, India.** His death is also termed as** Parinirvana, **the final Nirvana. After his death, the Buddha's teachings were collected into written form, called **Tripitaka (Three Baskets),** forming the foundation of Buddhist philosophy and practice.

questions.question: If 45% of 150 + x% of 170 = 40% of 317.5 , find the value of 'x'.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Convert percentages directly to decimals for quick multiplication:

45% of 150 = 0.45 × 150 = 67.5

40% of 317.5 = 0.4 × 317.5 = 127

Substitute these values directly into the given equation:

67.5 + 1.7x = 127 ⇒ 1.7x = 59.5 ⇒ x = 35

**∴ The correct answer is 35.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

45% of 150 + x% of 170 = 40% of 317.5

**Formula Used:**

P% of y = (P ÷ 100) × y

**Calculations:**

⇒ (45 ÷ 100) × 150 + (x ÷ 100) × 170 = (40 ÷ 100) × 317.5

⇒ 0.45 × 150 + x × 1.7 = 0.40 × 317.5

⇒ 67.5 + 1.7x = 127

⇒ 1.7x = 127 − 67.5

⇒ 1.7x = 59.5

⇒ x = 59.5 ÷ 1.7

⇒ x = 35

**∴ The correct answer is 35.**

**__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

Always follow the order of Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction. In simplifications, 'of' signifies multiplication and must be calculated before addition.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Converting percentages to fractions or decimals simplifies equations. For example, 40% = 40 ÷ 100 = 2/5 or 0.40. Using decimals directly avoids tedious LCM calculations.

Decimal Shifting Trick

Calculating P% of y is the same as calculating y% of P. You can dynamically shift decimals to make numbers easier: 40% of 317.5 is identical to 4 × 31.75 = 127.

questions.question: Let x be the least number which when divided by 15, 18, 20 and 27, the remainder in each case is 10 and x is a multiple of 31. What least number should be added to x to make it a perfect square?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

LCM of 15, 18, 20, 27 is 540, so x is of the form 540k + 10.

Since x is divisible by 31, the remainder of (540k + 10) ÷ 31 must be 0 ⇒ 13k + 10 is a multiple of 31.

By trial, the least integer value is k = 4, giving x = 540 × 4 + 10 = 2170.

The next perfect square after 2170 is 47² = 2209, so the required number to add is 2209 − 2170 = 39.

**∴ The correct answer is 39.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors = 15, 18, 20, and 27

Remainder = 10 in each case

x is a multiple of 31.

**Formula Used:**

x = (LCM of Divisors) × k + Remainder

**Calculations:**

⇒ LCM of 15, 18, 20, 27 = 540

⇒ Let the number be x = 540k + 10

⇒ x must be divisible by 31. We can split 540k as (31 × 17k + 13k).

⇒ So, x = 31 × 17k + 13k + 10

⇒ For x to be a multiple of 31, the remaining term (13k + 10) must be a multiple of 31.

⇒ Let us check for minimum integer values of k:

⇒ For k = 1: 13(1) + 10 = 23 (Not divisible by 31)

⇒ For k = 2: 13(2) + 10 = 36 (Not divisible by 31)

⇒ For k = 3: 13(3) + 10 = 49 (Not divisible by 31)

⇒ For k = 4: 13(4) + 10 = 62 (Divisible by 31, as 62 = 31 × 2)

⇒ Substitute k = 4 into our original equation for x:

⇒ x = 540 × 4 + 10 = 2160 + 10 = 2170

⇒ We need to add the least number to x to make it a perfect square.

⇒ Checking nearby perfect squares: 46² = 2116 and 47² = 2209

⇒ The least perfect square strictly greater than 2170 is 2209.

⇒ Least number to be added = 2209 − 2170 = 39

**∴ The correct answer is 39.**

**__Additional Information__**

LCM and Remainder Concept

When a number is divided by multiple divisors a, b, and c leaving the same remainder R in each case, the general form of the number is given by LCM(a, b, c) × k + R, where k is an integer.

Finding the Nearest Perfect Square

To find the least number to add to a value N to make it a perfect square, find the square root of N, round it up to the next whole integer, calculate its square, and finally subtract N from the result.

Divisibility Simplification Method

When checking the divisibility of a large algebraic expression like Ak + B by a prime number P, we can divide A by P and use the remainder to simplify the equation, heavily reducing the calculation time and effort required.
</p

questions.question: Remainder when 59²⁸ divided by 7?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

59 divided by 7 leaves a remainder of 3.

According to Fermat's Little Theorem, ap−¹ ≡ 1 (mod p).

Here p = 7, so 3⁶ ≡ 1 (mod 7).

We need 3²⁸ = (3⁶)⁴ × 3⁴ ≡ 1 × 81 (mod 7).

81 divided by 7 leaves a remainder of 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = 59²⁸ ÷ 7

**Method Used:**

Cyclicity theorem: Remainders of powers of a number repeat in a fixed cycle.

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, we find the remainder when the base 59 is divided by 7.

⇒ 59 ÷ 7 leaves a remainder of 3.

⇒ Therefore, finding the remainder of 59²⁸ ÷ 7 is the same as finding the remainder of 3²⁸ ÷ 7.

⇒ Now, let us check the cycle of remainders for powers of 3 divided by 7:

⇒ 3¹ = 3 → Remainder is 3

⇒ 3² = 9 → Remainder is 2 (since 9 − 7 = 2)

⇒ 3³ = 27 → Remainder is 6 (since 27 = 7 × 3 + 6)

⇒ 3⁴ = 81 → Remainder is 4 (since 81 = 7 × 11 + 4)

⇒ 3⁵ = 243 → Remainder is 5 (since 243 = 7 × 34 + 5)

⇒ 3⁶ = 729 → Remainder is 1 (since 729 = 7 × 104 + 1)

⇒ The remainders repeat every 6 powers (Cyclicity = 6).

⇒ Now, divide the exponent 28 by the cyclicity 6.

⇒ 28 ÷ 6 = 4 with a remainder of 4.

⇒ The remainder will be the same as the remainder of 3⁴ ÷ 7.

⇒ From our pattern above, 3⁴ leaves a remainder of 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

**__Additional Information__**

Fermat's Little Theorem

If p is a prime number and a is an integer not divisible by p, then ap−¹ leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by p.

Cyclicity (Power Cycle)

The remainder of a number raised to successive powers repeats after a certain interval called cyclicity. Dividing the exponent by this cycle helps reduce huge exponents easily.

Euler's Totient Theorem

A generalization of Fermat's theorem: aφ⁽ⁿ⁾ ≡ 1 (mod n) where a and n are coprime, and φ(n) is the number of coprime integers up to n.
</p

Profit (P) = 21%

questions.question: If x = b + c, y = c - a, z = a - b, then find the value of x² + y² + z² - 2xy - 2xz + 2yz.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The given mathematical expression directly matches an algebraic identity.

x² + y² + z² − 2xy − 2xz + 2yz = (x − y − z)²

Substitute the given variable values into the term (x − y − z):

⇒ (b + c) − (c − a) − (a − b) = b + c − c + a − a + b = 2b

⇒ (2b)² = 4b²

**∴ The correct answer is 4b².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ x = b + c

⇒ y = c − a

⇒ z = a − b

**Formula Used:**

⇒ (p + q + r)² = p² + q² + r² + 2pq + 2qr + 2pr

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let us evaluate the given expression: x² + y² + z² − 2xy − 2xz + 2yz

⇒ Comparing this with our standard formula, we take p = x, q = −y, and r = −z.

⇒ This simplifies our original expression cleanly to: (x − y − z)²

⇒ Next, we substitute the given expressions for x, y, and z into (x − y − z):

⇒ x − y − z = (b + c) − (c − a) − (a − b)

⇒ Distribute the negative signs and open the brackets:

⇒ x − y − z = b + c − c + a − a + b

⇒ Cancel out the opposite terms (+c − c) and (+a − a) and group together:

⇒ x − y − z = 2b

⇒ Finally, substitute this result back into the squared identity expression:

⇒ (x − y − z)² = (2b)² = 4b²

**∴ The correct answer is 4b².**

**__Additional Information__**

Trinomial Expansion Identity

The fundamental identity for the square of a sum of three variables is represented as (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca.

Sign Variations in Expansion

By assigning negative signs to the variables, we derive adapted identities depending on the requirements. For instance, (a − b − c)² = a² + b² + c² − 2ab + 2bc − 2ca.

Important Cubic Identity

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca). Notably, if a + b + c = 0, the equation cleanly reduces to a single relation: a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.

questions.question: The area of a semicircle is 77 cm². Calculate its perimeter (in cm).

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a semicircle, the area is (1/2) × π × r² = 77 cm².

⇒ (1/2) × (22/7) × r² = 77 ⇒ (11/7) × r² = 77 ⇒ r² = 49 ⇒ r = 7 cm.

The perimeter of a semicircle can be calculated directly as (36/7) × r (since π + 2 = 22/7 + 14/7 = 36/7).

⇒ Perimeter = (36/7) × 7 = 36 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of the semicircle = 77 cm²

**Formula Used:**

Area of a semicircle = (1/2) × π × r²

Perimeter of a semicircle = π × r + 2 × r

**Calculations:**

⇒ (1/2) × (22/7) × r² = 77

⇒ (11/7) × r² = 77

⇒ r² = 77 × 7 ÷ 11

⇒ r² = 7 × 7 = 49

⇒ r = √49 = 7 cm

Now, calculate the perimeter of the semicircle:

⇒ Perimeter = r × (π + 2)

⇒ Perimeter = 7 × (22/7 + 2)

⇒ Perimeter = 7 × (36/7)

⇒ Perimeter = 36 cm

Circle Properties

The area of a full circle is πr² and its total circumference is 2πr.

Semicircle Perimeter

Unlike the area, the perimeter of a semicircle includes the straight diameter edge. Total Perimeter = πr + 2r.

Quadrant of a Circle

A quadrant is one-fourth of a full circle. Its Area = πr²/4 and its Perimeter = πr/2 + 2r.
